beats.text: Why do GPUs sit idle during LLM inference until Attention Is All You Need unlocks 41.8 throughput?
beats.visual_focus: A timeline of sequential tokens creeping forward one single block at a time while surrounding GPU cores sit in dim stasis.

visual_blueprint.title: SEQUENTIAL QUEUE BOTTLENECK
visual_blueprint.sub: O(N) sequential dependency stalls parallel compute

motif_params.title: SEQUENTIAL QUEUE BOTTLENECK
motif_params.sub: O(N) sequential dependency stalls parallel compute

beats.text: Recurrence created a brutal sequential bottleneck, acting like a factory assembly line where thousands of parallel processors sit idle waiting for baton handoffs.
beats.visual_focus: A single conveyor belt forcing a long line of robotic arms to freeze until a single serialized signal crawls across each step.

visual_blueprint.title: RNN SERIAL DEPENDENCY
visual_blueprint.sub: Hidden state h_t strictly requires h_{t-1}

motif_params.title: RNN SERIAL DEPENDENCY
motif_params.sub: Hidden state h_t strictly requires h_{t-1}

beats.text: The Transformer destroyed this bottleneck by discarding recurrence and convolutions entirely, attending to every token in the sequence simultaneously across parallel geometric space.
beats.visual_focus: The linear queue shatters into an all-to-all interconnected geometric matrix where every token connects instantly to every other token.

beats.text: Query vectors calculate dot-products against Key vectors to determine dynamic attention weights, retrieving Value representations instantly through pure, high-throughput matrix operations without sequential loops.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard schematic showing Query matrix multiplied by transposed Key matrix, scaled by square root of d_k, projecting Value weights in one step.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook got me immediately—framing RNNs as wasting thousands of GPU cores on a single thread hit home right away as a CS student. Beats 1 through 3 make the parallel vs. sequential concept super clear without talking down to me. Beat 4 drops Query, Key, and Value pretty fast, but explaining it as 'pure parallel matrix math replacing memory loops' brought it right back. In Beat 5, 'BLEU score' is raw NLP jargon that might make a freshman pause for a second, but the context makes it obvious it was a state-of-the-art benchmark.
